messages:
ravi: Heads-up — partner support handoffs for Marketplace integrators are messy. We had another late-night pager last night where nobody was sure who should open the joint war room. Can we define a short, deterministic SEV path?

sarah_pm: +1. This has bitten us twice. My ask: 1) a single shared channel to go to first, 2) an auto-created bridge, 3) clear oncall ownership windows.

ben_oncall: Suggestion: /create-bridge partner-<org>-sev that 1) creates a private war room channel, 2) pings both Redwood and partner oncall, 3) posts a link to the runbook. We already have the bot command but it's not used consistently.

partner_oncall_bot: /create-bridge accepted — channel #warroom-partner-acme-2087654321 created. Joining participants: @ben_oncall, @juan_partner_se. Zoom: https://meet.redwood/abc123. Runbook: https://confluence.redwood/partnerships/sev-quickpath

kate_sre: Can we standardize the escalation tree inside the bridge? Minimal required info: impact (prod/infra), affected customers, remediation steps attempted, snapshot of logs (paste GCP/AZ/console snippets), and a mitigation owner. Keep it to a checklist so partner and Redwood responders aren't asking for the same thing.

juan_partner_se: From the partner side: please include a single relay contact (partner oncall email) + SSO-safe artifact location (we can't share internal tickets). We can publish a short status note to our customer-facing page if you provide the template.

ravi: Draft process proposal: 
- Step 0: Partner notices suspect SEV -> posts in #partner-escalations (shared channel) with one-line impact + urgency tag (P0/P1)
- Step 1: Running /create-bridge in shared channel -> auto war room + bot posts runbook link & Zoom + notifies both oncall teams
- Step 2: Triage owner from whichever org created the bridge (explicit "owner" field in first message)
- Step 3: If no owner assigned within 10m, the oncall for the product (Redwood) auto-claims via :rotating_light: reaction and then coordinates
- Step 4: Regular 10m status updates in the war room; clear handback when RCA actions exist or incident closed

ben_oncall: I want to tweak Step 3: make timeout configurable per partner (some partners have slower auth rotations). Default 10m, but partner-specific TTL allowed. Also add an explicit escalation to SRE lead after 30m.

kate_sre: Agree. Add a short template that the bot injects when the bridge is created: 
```
Impact: 
Scope: 
First mitigation tried: 
Owner: 
Next escalation ETA: 
Checkpoint cadence: 10m
```

juan_partner_se: We'll commit to monitoring for the first 30m and will provide our customer status cadence. Also, can we add a short "handback summary" step so partner support knows what to do after Redwood closes?

ravi: Yes — handback summary is required. Bot will auto-generate a handback checklist when the incident is marked resolved.

sarah_pm: Next actions: 1) Ben to update bot with default bridge template (ETA: 48h). 2) Kate to add the partner-specific TTL config to runbook (ETA: EOW). 3) Juan to confirm partner oncall contact format and public status template (ETA: EOW). 4) Ravi to circulate the one-pager + diagram.

ben_oncall: I'll open a tiny PR to the bot repo with the template today. pinging @kate_sre for review.

partner_oncall_bot: Reminder scheduled: "Review partnership SEV quickpath" set for 48h.

ravi: Thanks — hoping this reduces noisy midnights. If anyone sees gaps in the steps above, call them out here. :pray:
